articles.detail: 5 cycles, all completed; avg 11 published per cycle (54 vs 62 yesterday); 0 quarantined

topSourceShare.source: Dawn, Al Jazeera Online and TRT World (tied)

experiment: Skipped. Multi-source, US datelines and Latin America datelines missed their targets, but the pause gate (`noNewExperimentsUntil` 2026-11-05) bars a new experiment and none is active. Nothing was evaluated or changed.
weakestArea: Latin America is furthest from target at 2% against 5%: Corumbá was the only dateline, after 7% yesterday and at least 5% on each of the seven days before, so this is one low day rather than a trend. US datelines reached 30% with the midterms three days out, though the metric's bounding box counts Témiscaming, Quebec as US; the true share is 15 of 54, or 28%, still over the 25% ceiling. Multi-source fell to 26% from 33% as reported yesterday; the 05:00, 10:00, 14:00 and 22:00 selectors each landed 0 or 1 economy multi-source picks against a floor of 2 and said the feed had too few.
watching: Hormuz: over 30 ship attacks in October set a record, Iran says it would reopen the strait within 2 days of a deal on its own route, and the Guards claim a fourth tanker fire that no other source confirms.
Iran: Khamenei ordered retaliation plans without geographic limits, while Iranian media say Vance's letter is unanswered and a Qatari delegation is in Tehran.
Binance: it says 90% of the $6.3 billion stolen has been replaced, withdrawals reopen on 1 November and cryptographic proof of reserves is due on 3 November.
Moscow: the US warned of a mass-casualty attack at Tsaritsyno on Saturday, and neither government has named a suspect.
Western Sahara: rival US and Russian resolutions failed with the UN mission's mandate expiring Saturday, and Morocco says UN personnel should leave.
US midterms: Newsom warned judges that federal agents may seize ballots, three days before the vote.
Nigeria: laboratory results on 2 suspected Ebola cases in the northeast decide whether there is an outbreak; no date has been given.
Ukraine: Congress reviews the 500-missile Patriot sale with delivery possibly years off, and Turkey has promised to raise the grain corridor with Russia.
coverageGaps: "Iran Offers Faster Hormuz Reopening" says traffic is "19% below the normal 4" ships a day. That normal is the indicator's 90-day average, taken from this year's disrupted months rather than ordinary traffic, so the sentence likely understates how far the strait has fallen, and the indicator row hands the writer a field called `normal`.
The Binance dateline is a guess: the editor log says no source places the story anywhere, so it added Washington to avoid quarantine. That also adds a US dateline to the count.
Four datelines name a country (China ×3, United States) and one names a state (Ohio), down from seventeen such datelines yesterday; the missing-dateline metric catches none of them.

Science reached 4 against the target of 5, with no disaster filler. Four of 5 cycles ran under the floor of 2, and the 10:00 selector said it passed over Scientific Reports papers and thin items, which points to science sources rather than the floor.

Tech's 13 is generous: two stories filed there are chiefly political or military (the US-Hungary antifa pact, air defence at Mar-a-Lago), and the 10:00 and 14:00 selectors said they took weak company features to reach the floor.
No Oceania dateline ran today, and Africa had 3, all from Nigeria (Abuja, Enugu, Minna).
Three stories rest only on state media or advocacy outlets: the Hami solar plant, Iran's Hormuz offer and the Guards' tanker claim, all labelled in the body.
context: Today's figures are provisional: the 05:00 cycle on 10-31 added 5 articles dated 10-30, which took yesterday from the 57 audited to 62 and its multi-source share from 33% to 35%, so today's count may rise the same way. Freshness (0.1-day median), duplicates and source concentration stayed healthy, with 42 outlets and none above 11%. The pause holds until 2026-11-05 while the stage runner cuts over; no tunable parameter covers the dateline or "normal" wording issues, so they are recorded for the operator.
